title: What an MLP Can Carve
tagline: A single line can only cut a plane in two. Add a hidden layer and the boundary bends into whatever shape the data needs.
summary: A live 2-D classification playground. Pick XOR, two circles, spirals, or moons; choose a width and activation; then press Train and watch a from-scratch MLP carve a curved decision region out of the plane, one gradient step at a time. Flip on the linear model to see a straight line fail on everything but the easy cases. The punchline you can feel: hidden units bend a line into arbitrary regions.
highlights: Train a real 2-layer MLP in your browser, from scratch, and watch the decision boundary converge live as gradient descent runs.
Switch between XOR, concentric circles, two spirals, and moons — each generated deterministically so the demo is reproducible.
Toggle a linear model to see a straight line collapse on XOR and spirals, the way Minsky and Papert warned in 1969.
Sweep the hidden width from 2 to 16 and feel the boundary gain more folds — more units means more pieces of line to stitch together.
Compare tanh and ReLU activations: smooth curves versus piecewise-linear creases carving the same data.
